shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving with rounded raised contours
horizontal band/register dividing upper from lower zones
curved arc or crescent-like motifs in the upper zone
elongated sinuous forms (arm-like / snake-like) descending the front face
justification: Both are tall upright stone slabs bearing shallow, rounded low relief organised into an upper zone of arc-like motifs, a horizontal banded divider, and a lower zone of long sinuous elements terminating near a raised disc, which gives a broadly comparable vertical scheme. The decisive difference is subject and treatment: A is a volumetric anthropomorphic sculpture with a modelled head and body whose reliefs read as arms, belt and ornaments, whereas B is a flat-faced pillar covered with distinctly zoomorphic figures (quadrupeds, a bird, a lizard-like creature) in a looser, more pictorial arrangement.
